Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 81, verse 1–14:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Takwir (The Folding Up), because it opens with mention of the sun and what happens to it on the Day of Resurrection of takwir (تكوير), which is: gathering parts of it together, so that it is wrapped up, its light is taken away, and it is cast down.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Depicting the Resurrection: by mentioning some of the terrors that will occur on it, and the changes in the cosmos that will precede it, in the sun, the stars, the mountains, the seas and the earth, so that nothing remains unchanged out of the awe of what happens on that dreadful day.

• Discussing revelation: by describing the angel who carries it, the description of the Prophet (ﷺ) who receives it, the exaltation of the status of the Qur'an, and the clarification of the falsehood of the claims of the polytheists about it and about the Noble Messenger who brought it.

[The Tafsir]

When the sun is wrapped up and its light is gone; and when the stars scatter and their light is extinguished; and when the mountains are set in motion away from the surface of the earth and become scattered dust; and when pregnant she-camels are abandoned and neglected; and when wild animals are gathered together and mixed up, so that God may exact retribution from some of them for others; and when the seas are set ablaze, becoming, despite their vastness, a blazing fire; and when souls are paired with their likes and counterparts; and when the buried baby girl is asked on the Day of Resurrection, a question meant to console her and to rebuke her killer: for what sin was she buried?; and when the scrolls of deeds are unrolled; and when the sky is stripped away and removed from its place; and when the Fire is kindled and set blazing; and when Paradise, the abode of bliss, is brought near to its righteous people: when all this occurs, every soul will know for certain what it has sent forward of good or evil.

Muhammad (ﷺ) certainly saw Jibril (Gabriel), who brings him the message, in his true form in which Allah created him, on the great horizon to the east, at Makkah. This was the first vision, which took place at the Cave of Hira. Muhammad (ﷺ) is not stingy in conveying the revelation. And this Qur'an is not the word of an accursed devil, expelled from the mercy of Allah, but the speech and revelation of Allah.

Where, then, will your minds lead you in denying the Qur'an after these decisive proofs? It is nothing but a reminder from God to all people, for whoever among you wishes to stand upright upon the truth and faith. Yet you cannot will uprightness, nor can you attain it, except by the will of God, Lord of all creatures.
